scope: Proposition 5.1 (Exact gas representation) of the manuscript “Signed cylinder propagation and marked polygons on the honeycomb lattice” (preprints/Signed-cylinder-propagation-and-marked-polygons-on-the-honeycomb-lattice-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2dda2109318f92bb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 49-50. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix d− < 0 < d in the respective nonzero displacement ranges of Theorem 6.1, with 0 < |d−| < d < 1/2. Fix also a compact set Ω ⊂ C of values of θ. 49 There is an integer T0, independent of m, such that for every integer T ≥ T0 and every finite integer m ≥ 0, the gas (5.39) converges absolutely, uniformly for θ ∈ Ω at that m, T, and satisfies Cm,T = c(T)em2κT Zm,T , c(T) = p 8/9 8 √ 2T Dℓ √ TDW ZΓ !2 Dg, Dℓ = X j∈8Z e−4πj2/T . (5.40) In particular it holds along T = bn for any fixed integer block length b ≥ T0 and every positive integer n. This common period domain allows T to remain fixed while m varies through finite integers. The absolute bounds may depend on m, T and the fixed displacements; no bound uniform in m or limiting assertion as d− ↑ 0 or d ↓ 0 is made.
